artifacts.summary: 7-phase, 5-wave plan for the manifest-declared topic/task_type-keyed post-task observer seam: resolve-all matching in manifest-routing-lib.sh, run-task-observers.sh invoker with bounded timeout and rc events, regression suite, correctly-ordered orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh call site, check-extension-docs.sh Rule X, and the guide/schema documentation making active_projects[].topic a dispatch-matching key.

memory_candidates.content: A shared first-match-wins resolver ladder cannot be reused for a fan-out (notify-all) seam. When a new feature needs 'every declaration that matches', add a SIBLING resolve-all function to the same library -- reusing its enumeration and prefix-match idioms -- rather than widening the existing single-value ladder's return contract. Measured instance: manifest-routing-lib.sh's routing_lookup/routing_lookup_flat return exactly one winning value via two globals; an observer seam that must invoke every matching extension's script would have silently dropped all matches but the first. Corollary for match-key selection: before keying a dispatch mechanism on task_type, check whether the real corpus actually carries that task_type -- a 17-task topic-grouped corpus had task_type lean4/general/typst and NONE matching its own topic, so a task_type-keyed observer would have matched nothing it existed to observe.
